title: Question 3
stem:
One end of the wire is clamped at C and a marker is attached to the wire above a scale S. A force to extend the wire is applied by attaching masses to the other end of the wire.
The reading X of the marker on the scale S is determined for different forces F applied to the end of the wire. The variation with X of F is shown in Fig. 3.2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The length of the wire from C to the marker for F = 0 is 3.50 m. The diameter of the wire is
0.38 mm.
Use the gradient of the line in Fig. 3.2 to determine the Young modulus E of the material of the wire in TPa.
$E = TPa $

markscheme_points.text: E = stress / strain or (F / A) / (e / l)
E (= 1.3 × 1011) = 0.13 TPa (allow answers in range 0.120-0.136 TPa)

hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using Hooke's law and Young modulus.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
Identify the core physical principle governing this problem: Hooke's law and young modulus. State the relevant formula or theoretical relationship clearly.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Substitute the known quantities into the formula with correct SI units and powers of ten:
$$E = stress / strain or (F / A) / (e / l); = [gradient × 3.5] / [π × (0.19 × 10-3)2] e.g. E = [{(40 - 5) / ([11.6 - 3.2] × 10-3)} × 3.5] / [π × (0.19 × 10-3)2] or [4170 × 3.5] / [π × (0.19 × 10-3)2]; E (= 1.3 × 1011) = 0.13 TPa (allow answers in range 0.120-0.136 TPa)$$
Work through the intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
